policies.title: Spanish ordinary passports: Central African Republic advance visitor visa
policies.summary: MAEC directs Spanish visitors to obtain the Central African Republic visa in Paris before travel.
conditions: This records the ordinary Spanish-passport visitor baseline, not work, residence, diplomatic, service or special-document treatment.
Admission, security, health and documentary requirements remain separately applicable.

policies.title: Spanish ordinary passports: Chad advance visitor visa
policies.summary: MAEC says ordinary-passport visa applications must be made online before travel; it does not establish electronic issuance.
conditions: From 11 May 2026 ordinary-passport applications must be made on Chad’s official website, and visas not processed online no longer permit entry.
Online application is not normalized as eVisa issuance; a valid entry visa is required before travel.

policies.title: Spanish ordinary passports: Republic of Congo advance visitor visa
policies.summary: MAEC says Spanish visitor visa applications are handled by the Republic of Congo Embassy in Paris.
conditions: This is an advance embassy route, not border or electronic issuance.
Purpose, documents, health, security and final admission remain applicable.

policies.title: Spanish ordinary passports: Liberia advance visitor visa
policies.summary: MAEC says Spanish passports need a Liberian visa and that it cannot be obtained at the airport.
conditions: MAEC directs travellers to the Liberian Honorary Consulate in Madrid for the visa.
This excludes residence, work, special documents and final admission.

policies.title: Spanish ordinary passports: Mali advance visitor visa
policies.summary: MAEC says Mali does not issue foreign visitors visas at the border and requires personal mission application.
conditions: The ordinary visitor visa must be requested from the Mali embassy or consulate responsible for the traveller’s residence.
Work, residence, special documents and final admission remain separate.

policies.title: Spanish ordinary passports: Niger advance visitor visa
policies.summary: MAEC says Spanish travellers obtain Niger’s entry visa at the Embassy in Brussels and cannot obtain it at airport or land border.
conditions: The exceptional invitation-based flying-visa procedure is conditional and does not displace the normal advance embassy baseline.
Security, purpose, documents and final admission remain applicable.

policies.title: Spanish ordinary passports: Sudan advance visitor visa
policies.summary: MAEC requires Spanish passport holders to obtain Sudan’s visa in advance from its Embassy in Spain.
conditions: The source expressly excludes airport issuance and advises allowing up to five weeks.
Registration after arrival, purpose, document and final-admission requirements remain separate.

policies.title: Spanish ordinary passports: Syria electronic visitor visa
policies.summary: Current MAEC guidance expressly identifies Syria’s evisa.sy electronic-visa route for Spanish visitors.
conditions: An ordinary visitor may instead use a visa issued by the Syrian Embassy; this policy records the expressly available electronic route.
Diplomatic and international-organisation visas require the Embassy and are excluded.

policies.title: Spanish ordinary passports: Burkina Faso electronic visitor visa
policies.summary: MAEC states that Burkina Faso entry and stay visas are issued primarily electronically through the official platform.
conditions: The eVisa must be printed and presented on arrival; the separate online travel form is not a visa.
Border issuance is not an ordinary Spanish-passport route.

policies.title: Spanish ordinary passports: Côte d’Ivoire airport-issued visitor visa
policies.summary: MAEC says Spain’s online pre-enrolment process culminates in issuance of the visitor visa at Abidjan airport.
conditions: Print and carry the approved pre-enrolment certificate; it must be shown to the airline and at Abidjan airport.
The online request is not electronic issuance: after confirmation, the visa is issued at the airport.

policies.title: Spanish ordinary passports: South Sudan advance visitor visa
policies.summary: MAEC directs Spanish visitors to obtain South Sudan’s visa through a South Sudan embassy before travel.
conditions: MAEC recommends the Embassy in Paris accredited to Spain and notes that processing may take days.
Its mention of an online application platform does not establish electronically issued visas and is noted as technically unreliable.

policies.title: Spanish ordinary passports: Bangladesh advance visitor visa
policies.summary: MAEC requires Spanish travellers departing from Spain to apply for Bangladesh’s visitor visa at its Embassy in Madrid.
conditions: The visa-on-arrival facility is only described for a traveller departing from a country without a resident Bangladesh embassy, and MAEC warns it is often refused to Spanish travellers from Spain.
This records the ordinary Spanish visitor baseline from Spain, excluding that conditional third-country itinerary.

policies.title: Spanish ordinary passports: Guinea-Bissau advance visitor visa
policies.summary: MAEC says Spanish visitors should travel with a Guinea-Bissau visa issued at origin through the embassy’s consular section.
conditions: The source describes online processing as paralysed and border visas as unclear and unstable; neither is the normal ordinary visitor baseline.
Purpose, documents and final admission remain applicable.

policies.title: Spanish ordinary passports: Jordan arrival visitor visa
policies.summary: MAEC expressly permits Spanish visitors to obtain Jordan’s visa at named airports and most border points.
conditions: The standard visitor and tourist visas are single-entry and usually valid for 30 days.
Online routes and crossings subject to current operations remain separate.

policies.title: Spanish ordinary passports: Sierra Leone preapproved arrival visitor visa
policies.summary: MAEC says the Sierra Leone electronic application produces an authorisation for visa issuance on arrival at Lungi airport.
conditions: The traveller applies and pays online, then receives an authorisation; the visa itself is issued at Lungi airport.
The separate health and travel-information form is not a visa.

policies.title: Spanish ordinary passports: Palestinian-territory access via Israeli ETA-IL
policies.summary: MAEC says Spain is within the visa-exempt nationalities that must obtain Israel’s ETA-IL for the relevant access route to the Palestinian Territories.
conditions: The ETA-IL takes effect for access controlled by Israeli authorities; it is not a Palestinian visa.
Access to Gaza, West Bank crossings, permits, security controls, closures and final admission remain separately governed.

policies.title: Spanish ordinary passports: Guyana visa-free short visits
policies.summary: MAEC states that EU-member nationals, including Spanish nationals, need no Guyana visa for tourist stays under one month.
conditions: The visa waiver is limited to tourism stays shorter than 30 days.
Return ticket, passport, vaccination, extension and final-admission requirements remain applicable.

policies.title: Spanish ordinary passports: Panama visa-free short visits
policies.summary: MAEC expressly exempts Spanish citizens from Panama visas for tourism stays under 90 days.
conditions: The waiver is limited to tourist stays shorter than 90 days.
Passport validity, departure ticket, funds, health and final-admission requirements remain separate.

conflicts.explanation: MAEC says that, after online pre-enrolment, the visa is issued at Abidjan airport; filing online is not electronic issuance.
MAEC directs Spanish visitors to obtain the visa through a South Sudan embassy before travel; the online application reference does not establish eVisa issuance.
MAEC says Spanish travellers must apply at Bangladesh’s Embassy in Madrid; the conditional third-country departure facility is not the normal Spanish baseline.
MAEC advises travelling with a visa issued at origin and describes border issuance as unclear and unstable, not an ordinary visitor baseline.

unresolved.reason: Current MAEC guidance says a visa is needed and cannot be obtained at the border, but it does not establish an ordinary Spanish visitor issuance channel or an electronically issued route.
Current MAEC guidance says a tourist visa is required and travel is organised and controlled, but it does not establish its ordinary Spanish visitor issuance timing.

MAEC says Iran has not officially resumed visa-on-arrival and requires pre-application before travel, but does not establish whether the resulting ordinary Spanish tourist visa is electronically or mission-issued.
